modules.title: Introduction to Nationalism and the Independence Movement
modules.html:
Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo and the struggle for independence. This section covers introduction to nationalism and the independence movement.

Key points

  • Which conference finalizes the path to Nigeria's independence — The London Constitutional Conferences.
  • The 'Nationalism' in Nigeria after World War II was intensified by _____. — the return of educated veterans and the Atlantic Charter.
  • The 'Zikist Movement' was an auxiliary of the _____ party. — NCNC.
  • The 19th-century Jihad of Usman dan Fodio was primarily a _____ movement. — social and religious reform.
  • The Zikist Movement was formed to: — Defend Azikiwe/Fight for independence.

Worked examples

Q: Which conference finalizes the path to Nigeria's independence?
A: The London Constitutional Conferences — The London conferences (1953, 1957, 1958) settled the issues of regionalism, the minority question, and the date for independence.

Q: The 'Nationalism' in Nigeria after World War II was intensified by _____.
A: the return of educated veterans and the Atlantic Charter — West African soldiers returned with global awareness, and the Atlantic Charter's promise of self-determination inspired the push for independence.

examples.a: the return of educated veterans and the Atlantic Charter

quiz.q: Which conference finalizes the path to Nigeria's independence?
quiz.solution: The London conferences (1953, 1957, 1958) settled the issues of regionalism, the minority question, and the date for independence.

quiz.q: The 'Nationalism' in Nigeria after World War II was intensified by _____.
options: the return of educated veterans and the Atlantic Charter
the fall of the Berlin Wall
quiz.solution: West African soldiers returned with global awareness, and the Atlantic Charter's promise of self-determination inspired the push for independence.

quiz.q: The 'Zikist Movement' was an auxiliary of the _____ party.
quiz.solution: The Zikist Movement was the radical youth wing of the NCNC, advocating for 'militant' nationalism and the ideals of Nnamdi Azikiwe.

quiz.q: The 19th-century Jihad of Usman dan Fodio was primarily a _____ movement.
quiz.solution: The Jihad aimed to cleanse Islamic practice and address the social injustices of the Hausa kings.

quiz.q: The Zikist Movement was formed to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Defend Azikiwe/Fight for independence.

quiz.q: The movement that sought to unite all African people globally is called...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Pan-Africanism.

quiz.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is often described as _____.
quiz.solution: It was called quasi-federal because it provided for a central legislature and regional houses, but the center still held significant power over the regions.

quiz.q: The primary role of the 'Ogboni' society in many Yoruba kingdoms was _____.
options: checking the powers of the Alaafin and Oyomesi
quiz.solution: The Ogboni was a secret cult of elders that played a judicial role and balanced the power between the Alafin and the executive chiefs.

quiz.q: The 'Satiru Rebellion' of 1906 was a challenge against _____.
options: British colonial rule in Northern Nigeria
quiz.solution: The Satiru uprising near Sokoto was a Mahdist-inspired revolt against the British occupation and their Fulani allies.

quiz.q: The 1851 bombardment of Lagos was carried out by the British to remove _____.
quiz.solution: Kosoko supported the slave trade; the British ousted him and installed the pro-British Akintoye.

quiz.q: The 19th-century Yoruba Civil Wars were largely caused by _____.
options: the collapse of Old Oyo and the struggle for power
quiz.solution: Following the fall of Oyo, city-states like Ibadan, Abeokuta, and Ijaye fought for over 50 years for dominance (e.g., the Kiriji War).

quiz.q: The legendary priest who helped Osei Tutu found the Asante Empire was _____.
quiz.solution: Okomfo Anokye is credited with summoning the Golden Stool from heaven as a symbol of unity for the Asante clans.

quiz.q: The ancient Kanem-Borno Empire was located in the basin of Lake _____.
quiz.solution: Lake Chad was the strategic center for the Kanem-Borno Empire's power and trade.

quiz.q: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Usman Dan Fodio.

quiz.q: The NYSC was established by the regime of:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Yakubu Gowon.

quiz.q: Mary Slessor is remembered for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Stopping the killing of twins.

quiz.q: Nelson Mandela spent how many years in prison?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 27.

quiz.q: The Macpherson Constitution was in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 1951.

quiz.q: The fall of the Old Oyo Empire was caused by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Fulani Jihad and internal crisis.

quiz.q: The Golden Stool is associated with the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Asante (Ashanti).

quiz.q: The Egbe Omo Oduduwa was a cultural organization for the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Yoruba.

quiz.q: The Sokoto Caliphate founder:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Usman Dan Fodio.

quiz.q: Royal Niger Company received charter in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1886.

quiz.q: Capital moved to Abuja by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Babangida.

quiz.q: Kwame Nkrumah led:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Ghana.

quiz.q: According to tradition, the founder of the Hausa states was...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Bayajidda.

quiz.q: The 'June 12' 1993 election was widely believed to have been won by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Moshood Abiola.

quiz.q: The Oyo Empire was headed by the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Alaafin.

quiz.q: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca took place in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: 1324.

quiz.q: Nana of Itsekiri resisted the:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: British.
